newsitem.title: CHINA: HK businessman gives judge something to chew on.
newsitem.headline: HK businessman gives judge something to chew on.

text.p: A Hong Kong judge who fined a gum-chewing businessman and politician HK$500 (US$65) for contempt of court was herself given something to chew on.
Leung Ka-ching won an appeal against the fine, arguing that he had chewed gum in court in January only because he wanted to show his respect to the court "by having fresh breath".

His gum-chewing fine was reversed. The appeal judge said Leung's punishment was inappropriate and that Leung had not been allowed his basic defence rights. The former election candidate appeared in court in January on an illegal advertising charge.
Leung said he fought the penalty for his gum chewing on principle. "It's not the money," said Leung, who represented himself at Tuesday's appeal. "Everybody has $500 in Hong Kong."

"The magistrate was simply wasting the taxpayer's money. If she had asked me whether or not I wanted to plead guilty to chewing, I would have accepted her judgment," the South China Morning Post quoted him as saying.
